# What this study is

A drought is no longer read as a *deficit queue*. The retired queue study
(26 November 2026) asked whether an M/M/1/K backlog of irrigation claims adds
drought information beyond SSI-3, concurrently, in two regions with identical
assumed constants. It produced a small, partly unresolved effect, and an
external expert review diagnosed the three design causes that produced it:
the queue carried no information its benchmark lacked; the queue class was
wrong for a fluid storage process; and the utilisation screen selected on
assumed constants (`PIVOT.md` §1). **That study is retired as a
negative-result methods note; its numbers remain exactly as published in
`output/region_summary.csv` and git history.**

**Study P1** replaces the queue with what the hydrology literature has used
for seventy years (Moran 1954; Kendall 1957; Brutsaert 2008): a
**storage-deficit state** estimated from the catchment's own recession
behaviour and propagated by a mass-balance-verified fluid water balance. The
question is prospective: does this state improve probabilistic forecasts of
**hydrological drought** (SSI-3 ≤ −1) and **low-flow** events at **1, 3 and
6-month leads**, beyond persistence, lagged standard indices and an
antecedent precipitation index? **India (CAMELS-IND) is the study; the USA
(Caravan-US) runs the identical protocol as a declared transfer check, never
as a contrast.**

**Announced limitation (binding wording, PIVOT.md §4.1).** The storage state
is estimated from P, ET and Q of the same catchment record that builds the
indices; it is therefore a *different transform with different memory
properties*, not independent information. The confirmatory question is
exactly whether the physically-shaped transform (recession constants,
storage capacity, mass-balance dynamics) out-predicts the standardised
3-month boxcar that SSI-3 applies.

# Gate G2 — the corrected re-run (the retired design's acceptance gate)

Before P1 scoring could start (`AGENTS.md` rule), the retired design was
re-run once, corrected: **dataset PET** (GLEAM `pet_gleam`, shipped in
CAMELS-IND forcings; FAO Penman–Monteith in Caravan-US), the **measured
irrigated fraction** (`irrigation_frac`, CAMELS-IND anth attributes)
replacing the flat `f_irr = 0.10`, a **seasonal kharif/rabi Kc and effective-
rainfall φ** `[assumption: FAO-56-style two-season simplification]`, queue
thresholds computed on **training years only** (FQ4), the honest **memory
baselines** `ssi6`, `api`, `persistence` added (FQ1), the ridge penalty
**tuned per family** by calendar-block CV (FS3), and **BSS vs climatology**
reported (FS1). The decision rule below was frozen in `PIVOT.md` §3 *before*
the gate ran.

```{r gate-g2, eval=have("gateG2_summary.csv")}
g2 <- rd("gateG2_summary.csv")
if (!is.null(g2)) {
  g2p <- g2[baseline %in% c("persistence", "ssi6", "api", "bestof")]
  knitr::kable(g2p[, .(
    region, target, baseline, n,
    median_delta = sprintf("%+.4f", median_delta),
    CI = sprintf("[%+.4f, %+.4f]", boot_lo, boot_hi),
    sign = sprintf("%d/%d", sign_k, sign_n), sign_p = signif(sign_p, 2)
  )], caption = "Gate G2: median paired Brier delta of ssi3_plus_queue over each baseline (positive favours the queue), two-level bootstrap 95% interval, one-sided sign test. Source: output/gateG2_summary.csv.")
  dec <- if (have("gateG2_decision.txt")) {
    paste(readLines(OUT("gateG2_decision.txt")), collapse = " ")
  } else "(decision not yet written)"
  cat("\n**Gate G2 decision (frozen rule applied as written):**", dec, "\n")
}
```

```{r gate-g2-sample, eval=have("gateG2_sample_report.csv")}

The completeness rule (training-year day counts) retains far fewer Indian gauges than the literature expected; Study P1 therefore counts complete months instead (§4.2 of PIVOT.md). Source: output/gateG2_sample_report.csv.")

# Data

The data contract follows `PIVOT.md` §4.3. India: CAMELS-IND daily catchment-
mean forcings (precipitation, temperature, **GLEAM PET shipped in the
dataset**), observed streamflow, and attributes including the **measured
irrigated fraction** and land-cover fractions. USA (transfer check):
Caravan-US forcings with FAO Penman–Monteith PET. Missing streamflow days are
never interpolated; a month containing a missing day is excluded from
indices and targets. Zero-flow days are kept as recorded and treated as
**censored** observations on the storage path: recession segments start after
the last zero-flow day and the storage state sits at its floor through a
zero-flow spell. No gauge is dropped for a high zero-flow fraction alone.

# The storage engine (`R/functions/storage_engine.R`)

One fluid state, three fitted quantities, no queue artefacts. Fitted per
gauge on **training years (1981–2010) only**:

1. **Baseflow index** — Lyne–Hollick single-pass filter, `alpha = 0.925`
   `[assumption: standard value]`.
2. **Recession constant `k`** — on recession segments (≥ 10 consecutive days
   of strictly negative daily flow change with no rain day
   `[assumption: rain day ≥ 5 mm/day]`, censored at zero-flow days): per
   segment $\ln Q(t+1) - \ln Q(t) = -1/k$; median across segments. The
   low-flow nonlinearity exponent $p$ in $-dQ/dt = a\,Q^{p}$ is fitted on the
   pooled segment pairs and clipped to $[0.5, 1]$
   `[assumption: declared physical range]`.
3. **Storage scale `S_cap` (mm)** — storage-outflow inversion: with
   $Q_g = (K_a S)^{b_s}$ and $dS/dt = -Q_g$ along a recession, $b_s =
   1/(2-p)$ and $K_a = a/b_s$; $S_{cap}$ is the 95th percentile of the
   implied storage over the training segments. Gauges with fewer than
   `r P1_MIN_SEGMENTS` segments **borrow the basin-median** parameters and
   are flagged `borrowed_parameters`.

Propagated daily, no observed-Q input:

$$S(t+1) = \mathrm{clip}\big(S(t) + P_e(t) - E_a(t) - Q_g(t),\ 0,\ S_{cap}\big)$$
$$P_e(t) = \max(P(t) - \varphi_m(\mathrm{month})\,P(t), 0), \qquad
E_a(t) = \min(\mathrm{PET}(t)\,K_{c,m}(\mathrm{month}),\ S(t) + P_e(t))$$
$$Q_g(t) = \min\big((K_a\,S(t))^{b_s},\ S(t)\big)$$

Initialised at $S(0) = S_{cap}/2$ with a 2-year warm-up excluded from
features `[assumption]`. The state is millimetres of depth over the
catchment — no claims, no hectares; the unit wall (`units.R`) carries every
conversion. The **per-day ledger identity**
$S(t+1)-S(t) = P_e - E_a - Q_g - \mathrm{overflow} + \mathrm{deficit}$ holds
to floating point (checks V16–V19 of the battery; residual tolerance 1e−9).

# Screens, sample and power (PIVOT.md §4.2)

Screens are completeness and event-count only; the utilisation window is
gone. (1) record in the 1981–2020 window; (2) ≥ 30 complete training months
and ≥ 10 complete test months (a month is complete when every day is
present); (3) ≥ `r P1_MIN_TRAIN_EVENTS` target events in the training feature
years per target (dropped per target and reported); (4) recession quality:
≥ `r P1_MIN_SEGMENTS` segments of ≥ 10 days in training years — gauges
failing this are excluded from the storage families only, never from the
baselines, and the asymmetry is reported; (5) zero-flow rivers are kept with
censoring and the fraction is reported.

```{r p1-sample, eval=have("p1_sample_report.csv")}
s1 <- rd("p1_sample_report.csv")
if (!is.null(s1)) {

    read = .N,
    complete = sum(pass_complete),
    events_T1 = sum(pass_complete & pass_events_t1),
    events_T2 = sum(pass_complete & pass_events_t2),
    storage_scored = sum(pass_complete & pass_events_t1 & pass_recession),
    borrowed = sum(borrowed_parameters)
  )]
  agg$region <- "India"
  knitr::kable(agg, caption = "Sample report, India: n per screen stage. Source: output/p1_sample_report.csv.")
}
s2 <- rd("p1_sample_report_usa.csv")
if (!is.null(s2)) {

    read = .N,

    storage_scored = sum(pass_complete & pass_events_t1 & pass_recession),
    borrowed = sum(borrowed_parameters)
  )]
  agg$region <- "USA (transfer)"
  knitr::kable(agg, caption = "Sample report, USA transfer arm. Source: output/p1_sample_report_usa.csv.")
}
```

# Frozen evaluation protocol (PIVOT.md §4.5–§4.8)

- **Targets.** T1 (confirmatory): monthly SSI-3 ≤ −1, all months of a spell
  (the joint series). T2 (descriptive): monthly mean flow below the gauge's
  training-period daily Q90. Leads h ∈ {1, 3, 6} months, strictly
  prospective: a forecast issued at month *t* uses only information
  available at *t*; the strict split keeps every issue/target pair fully
  inside its window (no end-of-window leakage).
- **Families** (identical ridge machinery, penalty tuned per family by
  calendar-block CV inside the training years, grid and folds frozen in
  `R/config.R`): `climatology` (reference), `persistence` (target index at
  issue time), `lagged_indices` (SPI-3, SSI-3, SSI-6, SPI-6 at issue time),
  `api` (recursive antecedent index, decay 0.95 `[assumption]`, effective
  memory ≈ 90 days), `storage` (state anomaly, 1- and 3-month storage
  change, days since high flow, and the fitted attributes), and
  **`storage_plus_indices`** (the confirmatory family).
- **Confirmatory contrasts.** H1: `storage_plus_indices` vs the **frozen
  best-of** `{persistence, lagged_indices, api}` at **h = 3**; H2: same at
  **h = 6**; selected per gauge on training-year CV only, before any test
  scoring. H0 (descriptive, declared in advance): at h = 1 the storage
  family is expected to reach **parity**, and a null there is the predicted
  outcome.
- **Headline metric.** Brier skill score vs `climatology`; paired per-gauge
  Brier deltas on identical held-out months; two-level block bootstrap
  (years within gauges, then gauges; B = `r P1_BOOT_B`); one-sided sign test
  at ≥ 60 % consistency; harm bound `r P1_HARM_BOUND` Brier
  `[assumption: smallest season-scale change an operator would act on]` —
  gauges beyond it are listed in the outputs, never hidden behind a median.
- **Class-balance rule.** Gauge-target cells with a training positive rate
  below 2 % or above 98 % are flagged and excluded from Brier contrasts.
- **No model sees a test year until scoring, once, at the end.**

# Results

```{r p1-bss, eval=have("p1_bss.csv")}
b <- rd("p1_bss.csv")
if (!is.null(b)) {
  med <- b[is.finite(bss), .(bss_med = stats::median(bss)), by = .(family, lead, target)]
  tw <- dcast(med, family + target ~ lead, value.var = "bss_med")
  setnames(tw, c("1", "3", "6"), c("h=1", "h=3", "h=6"))
  knitr::kable(tw, digits = 4,
    caption = "Median Brier skill score vs climatology per family and lead (India). Positive = better than climatology. Source: output/p1_bss.csv.")
}
```

```{r p1-confirmatory, eval=have("p1_confirmatory.csv")}
cf <- rd("p1_confirmatory.csv")
if (!is.null(cf)) {
  knitr::kable(cf[, .(hypothesis, lead, n,
    median_delta = sprintf("%+.4f", median_delta),
    CI = sprintf("[%+.4f, %+.4f]", boot_lo, boot_hi),
    sign = sprintf("%d/%d", sign_k, sign_n),
    share = signif(sign_share, 2), verdict)],
    caption = "Confirmatory table, India: storage_plus_indices vs the frozen best-of memory baseline, SSI-3 <= -1 target. H0 at lead 1 is the predicted parity/null and is reported as such. Source: output/p1_confirmatory.csv.")
}
```

# Verification battery (gate G1)

`R/verify.R` carries `r 21` checks and must pass 21/21 before any run: the
frozen CTMC's exact-solution checks (V1–V7), the unit wall (V8–V9), the
catchment-relative thresholds (V10), the index standardisation (V11), the
metric hand cases (V12), the zero classifier and gap rule (V13–V14), the
G2 rate builder (V15), and the storage engine's checks — fluid ledger
identity with zero-flow pinning (V16), analytic recession vs propagator
(V17), recession-constant recovery (V18), storage-scale inversion (V19),
the leakage tripwire (V20), and the BSS hand case (V21). The three-way
agreement on the P1 path is: analytic recession solution ↔ fluid propagator
↔ daily mass-balance ledger.

# Reproducibility

Every output CSV is written by `R/study_gate_g2.R`, `R/study_p1.R`,
`R/power_check.R` or `R/figures_p1.R` through `write_csv_sidecar()`, so each
carries a JSON sidecar with the git hash, code hash, shape and R session.
Nothing in `output/` is hand-edited. The retired study's backbone
(`R/study.R`) is kept as the record; the frozen CTMC engine
(`R/functions/queue_engine.R`) is untouched and will be reused unchanged by
Study P3 (climate-projection queue reliability, CAMELS-IND-Proj).
